title.narrative: Second Lower Secondary Education for the Most Disadvantaged Areas Project

description.narrative: The project is a continuation of the first Lower Secondary Education for the Most Disadvantaged Regions Project, which has been successfully implemented and will be completed by the end of 2014. 2 The second project will help the Government of Viet Nam assist the poor and near-poor through the enhancement of lower secondary education (LSE), which contributes to an expansion of opportunities.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: More equitable access and retention of ethnic minorities, girls, and disadvantaged children in LSSs in northern midland and mountainous areas, central highlands, Mekong River Delta, and north central and central coastal areas, which are frequently affected by typhoons.

20,000 teacher and managers trained (10,000 female and 10,000 male). Achievement: 70,694 Progress/Status: Achieved. 70,694 teachers and education managers (41,467 are female, or 58.65%) participated in the training by August 2023. Of which: - The Project provided training to 19,088 teachers and education managers (9,391 are female). Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, training courses in 2021 were terminated. After the loan agreement was extended in December 2021 with reallocation, Viet Nam government did not allow using ODA loans for training and capacity building any more. - The provincial DOETs, BOETs and LSSs provided training in implementing local education materials under the 2018 General Education Program to 51,606 teachers and education managers (32,076 were female). Data Source: Survey by central PMU Actual value: 70,694

At least 29,700 more students accommodated (14,850 female and 14,850 male), and 3,780 accommodated in semi-boarding facilities (1,890 female and 1,890 male). Achievement: 92,219 Progress/Status: Achieved. By August 2023, 747 classrooms were completed and accommodated 92,219 students, including 45,734 female students (49.59%) and 32.531 EM students. (35.08%). By August 2023, 358 semi-boarding facilities have been constructed. 184 boarding rooms for female students. Decentralization of teaching and learning tools Indicator: About 4,000 LSS teachers in three disadvantaged areas, both male and female, receive training on the localized education materials. Achievement: 42,181 Progress/Status: Achieved. CPMU prepared bidding documents for the training on localized education materials. The training workshops were scheduled to take place in 2021. The Departments of Education and Training have been providing training in implementing the materials for grades 6, 7 and 8 to 42,181 teachers and education managers (29,363 are female).
According to the roadmap for implementing the General Education Program, the LEMs for grade 9 will be implemented in school year 2024-2025, which is after the Project ends. Therefore, data on teachers and education managers undergoing training in LEMs for grade 9 is not available. Data Source: MOET's education management information system Actual value: 42,181
